data.title: bn-32l: Prove paintop-to-Apollo64 sprite production loop

data.body: [medium] Make the production recipe fail closed on the exact-alpha invariant. `assert.alpha_valid@1` only checks that alpha is in range; `console sprite import --mapping exact` thresholds alpha, counts surviving partial-alpha pixels, and still exits successfully. A future edit can therefore validate and exact-import while silently changing transparent/opaque pixels. The current specimen does report `partial_alpha_pixels: 0`, but the documented command only prints that fact. Add a checked `jq -e`/script (also checking expected dimensions and palette indices), or an equivalent binary-alpha assertion, so this reusable production bridge rejects drift.

[medium] Keep this status statement consistent with the actual cart. The rebuild still renders the player through `draw_frog_pose` (defined at cart line 1797 and called at 2027) and the boss through `draw_buzzkill`; the checked 24x24 PNG is not imported into the committed cart. Rephrase this as the intended asset-production direction (which matches the following specimen caveat), or wire the atlas into gameplay before claiming the visual rebuild uses it instead of procedural actor primitives.

data.reason: The specimen itself reproduces exactly, but the reusable recipe does not fail closed on partial alpha and the design document inaccurately claims the current game has replaced procedural actors with the PNG bridge.

Independent review reproduced deterministic output and exact import, but blocks on two documentation/workflow defects: binary alpha is reported rather than enforced, and design.md claims sprite-atlas adoption that the procedural cart does not implement.

data.body: Fixed in 615f1a6. The documented pipeline now uses pipefail plus jq -e to reject wrong dimensions, resizing, palette drift, partial alpha, or a writing dry-run. The exact command was executed successfully against the specimen; the text now explicitly distinguishes alpha_valid numeric-range checking from binary-alpha enforcement.

Fixed in 615f1a6. The design now states that the rebuild will replace procedural actors and explicitly says both production-atlas work and runtime migration remain outstanding; it no longer claims the specimen is live in the cart.

data.reason: Re-reviewed 615f1a6. The documented jq/pipefail gate now enforces dimensions, no resize, exact palette indices, binary alpha, and non-writing import; it passes the specimen and rejects partial-alpha drift. The design text now accurately makes atlas/runtime migration future work. Two fresh paintop outputs remain byte-identical with the recorded hashes.
Fixed in 615f1a6 and re-verified: acceptance gate passes valid specimen and rejects partial-alpha drift.
Fixed in 615f1a6: wording accurately describes atlas and runtime migration as pending.
Clears the stale self-block accidentally recorded under the inherited author identity during independent review; substantive reviewer verdict is the console-review LGTM.
